page_title: Concurrent Servers: Part 6 - Callbacks, Promises and async/await

summary.title: Concurrent Servers: Part 6 - Callbacks, Promises and async/await
summary.one_liner: Learn how a Node.js primality-testing server evolves from nested callbacks to promises to async/await, and why each step eases asynchronous code.
takeaways: Node.js is single-threaded, so CPU-heavy work is offloaded to child processes via child_process.fork and handled with message callbacks.
Nested callbacks (callback hell) make data flow harder to follow and make error handling awkward because exceptions do not cross callback stack frames.
Promises flatten nested callbacks into a then chain and allow a single catch at the end for errors; util.promisify wraps callback APIs.
async/await lets asynchronous code read like straight-line blocking code while still registering callbacks and yielding to the event loop.
summary.summary: The article is part 6 of a series on writing concurrent network servers. It revisits the primality-testing server from part 4 (originally in C with libuv), rebuilding it in Node.js with a child process per computation and a Redis cache. Each version of onConnData is shown in turn: plain nested callbacks, promise chains with promisify, and finally async/await. The author discusses the downsides of callback nesting and continuation-passing style, including error handling, before concluding with the question of whether this model beats threads for high-load concurrency.
